entry.title: iPhone Duo-n’t
entry.content:
I went to see the new iPhone Duo today. I have been rather sceptical about the whole thing, but I assumed that once I held it in my hand, it would create the same kind of craving every other iPhone has.

When I first picked it up, it felt as if it might. I really liked the screen’s dimensions when closed. It felt new and fresh, different from the form factor Apple have played on repeat for so long. However, when trying to use it, I realised it’s way too wide to use comfortably with one hand while standing on the tube. And then, for the main trick, when opening the phone up to reveal the folded screen, the whole thing just felt like a slightly awkward iPad mini.

So no, iPhone Duo is not for me. I don’t get what it’s for. And at that price?

entry.title: Hello, Panasonic Lumix L10
entry.content:
I finally decided to get a real camera again after years of relying on my phone.

I went for the Panasonic Lumix L10, and it seems promising so far, but there are definitely a lot of buttons and options to learn. I seem to have forgotten pretty much everything about how to use a camera!

I don’t necessarily think I will take better photos with this camera than my phone. I know I’m the limitation, not the camera. What I’m hoping for, though, is photos that look a little bit more like photos, without the phone magically compensating for everything. I also think it will make me a slightly more intentional photographer.

And, tbh, I like the idea of being the type of person who carries an actual camera around! 😅

See below for some photos from my commute this evening, with everything just on auto-auto. No edits or filters.

entry.title: My Neighbour Totoro
entry.content:
It’s been a while since I went to the theatre, so I was rather excited to go and see My Neighbour Totoro the musical last night.

And what a treat it was! I sat absolutely fascinated, my mouth open, through most of it. The set design was incredibly clever, whether it was buildings being put together before our eyes or just some cornfields passing by.

I loved how the stage workers, if it’s fair to call them that, were sometimes part of the play, sometimes puppeteers and sometimes just doing what stage workers do.

And the puppets, of course! From the huge Totoro to a flock of chickens. I didn’t think they would do the cat bus, as it seemed too hard to me, but they did!

Definitely go and see it before it’s gone!

entry.title: Daytripping to Rye
entry.content:
It’s been a while since we went on a proper day trip, so after a bit of googling, we decided to head to Rye.

This medieval town is just an hour from London and turned out to be well worth a visit. Very picturesque and not too crowded, with lots of cute old houses lining small, cobbled streets. It’s fascinating, too, that it used to be a seaside town, but the sea is now 2 miles away!

I particularly enjoyed the view from the tower of the 900-year-old church, a beer in the garden of the Ypres Castle Inn and a nice lunch at The Union Rye.

A very nice day out!
